newsitem.title: UK: No stability pact could offset flawed EMU - Clarke.
newsitem.headline: No stability pact could offset flawed EMU - Clarke.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said no stability pact could hold together a single European currency zone if it was seriously flawed from the start.

"The consequences of a euro zone which is badly put together, or which contains seriously non-convergent countries, would be extremely damaging to all member states in the European Union," he told parliament.
"No stability pact -- no matter how strict, no matter how dire the punishment for transgressions -- could hold such a euro zone together."

If EMU was entered into by countries which were not sufficiently competitive or which were too inflexible in their economic structures to respond to pressures other than through devaluations, then it would set up "insupportable and damaging strains."
Clarke said any attempt to "fudge" the convergence criteria could be disastrous.
